finding_candidates.statement: Harer's virtual cohomological dimension for mapping class groups is vcd(Mod_{g,n}) = 4g-4+n for g>=1, n>0, and 4g-5 only for g>=2, n=0 (with n-3 for g=0, n>=3). The interpolated form 4g+n-5 used in ATT-0012 is the n=0 formula illegitimately extended and understates the vcd by exactly 1 for every n>=1; independent check: Mod_{1,1} = SL_2(Z) has vcd 1 = 4-4+1, not 4+1-5 = 0. For (g,n)=(6,6) the correct value is 26, so no vanishing is available in ordinary degree 26.

No cohomological-dimension argument can discharge any open input in the RED-0001 list. With the correct Harer vcd, the gap vcd(Mod_{g,n}) - (2d-16) for d=3g-3+n equals 18-2g-n when n>=1 and 17-2g when n=0, which is 0 for (3,12), (5,8), (6,6), (7,4), (8,2) and 1 for (8,0), (8,1). Hence the required ordinary degree 2d-16 never exceeds the vcd for any listed pair, and lands exactly on it for five of the seven: the reduction's unresolved inputs sit at the very top of the virtual cohomological dimension, which is structurally why they are hard. Any future attempt whose engine is degree-based vanishing (vcd, affineness, or homotopy-dimension bounds) can be rejected on arithmetic alone without examining its Hodge theory.

Evidence refining the FND-0001 identification: because M_{g,n} is smooth, the ordinary realisation W_{2d-16}H^{2d-16}(M_{g,n}) is the LOWEST weight piece of that cohomology group (weights of H^m on a smooth stack lie in [m, 2m]), and by Deligne it equals the image of H^{2d-16}(Mbar_{g,n}) -> H^{2d-16}(M_{g,n}). Two consequences for reviewing future attempts. Proving the full ordinary group vanishes is strictly stronger than the target and is therefore a legitimate but unnecessarily demanding route; and non-vanishing of the full group H^{2d-16}(M_{g,n}) does NOT refute the packet's expected Q(8), so a refuted vanishing argument must not be recorded as evidence against the target itself.

strongest_attack: The proof has exactly one novel step, and that step is numerically false. Step 3 / claim A4 asserts Harer's virtual cohomological dimension as vcd(Mod_{g,n}) = 4g+n-5 for g>=2, giving vcd(Mod_{6,6}) = 25 and hence H^26(M_{6,6};Q) = 0. Harer's theorem is 4g-5 only when n=0; for g>=1 and n>0 it is 4g-4+n. The attempt has grafted the unpunctured formula onto the punctured case, losing one degree. Correctly, vcd(Mod_{6,6}) = 4*6-4+6 = 26, which is exactly the ordinary degree the target lives in, so the dimension bound yields nothing precisely where it is needed and the vanishing in A5/A6 collapses. Everything else in the attempt survives scrutiny - the d=21 arithmetic, the Poincare identification H^BM_16 = H^26(21), the weight -16 and the Q(-13)(21)=Q(8) twist, the CKgP-range and base-case placement of (6,6), and the honest labelling of external inputs - which makes the off-by-one the sole load-bearing failure. Two independent corroborations, neither requiring outside literature. (i) Internal reductio: applying the attempt's own formula across the RED-0001 list discharges (3,12), (5,8), (6,6), (7,4) and (8,2) - five of the seven unresolved open inputs - by a 1986 theorem, which flatly contradicts OBS-0001's record that degree 16 is open as of May 2026 and would make the published reduction largely vacuous on arrival. (ii) Structural fingerprint: with the CORRECT formula, vcd - (2d-16) = 18-2g-n for n>=1 and 17-2g for n=0, which evaluates to 0 for (3,12), (5,8), (6,6), (7,4), (8,2) and to 1 for (8,0), (8,1). Every listed pair sits at or one below the vcd - the list is precisely the locus where dimension-counting cannot help, and the correct formula explains the list's shape while the attempt's does not. A secondary, non-fatal observation: the argument targets vanishing of the entire ordinary group H^26, which is strictly stronger than the required lowest-weight piece W_26 H^26; conversely, non-vanishing of H^26(M_{6,6}) would not refute the target, so this refutation of the argument is not a refutation of the packet's expected Q(8).
